analysis: Reviewed the single changed unit, provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDSharedProcessCheckpointTests.swift. The PR adds only a test, queuedWritesStayInsideHostLedger (head lines 147-188), and changes no production code. The test asserts that queued SSD write-behind donations keep their host IO-scratch reservations in the shared process ledger. With room for four writer reservations, a fifth donation is refused with a hostMemoryUnavailable outcome and no writeQueueFull outcome. After the barrier is released, the four queued donations complete and all charged bytes return to 0. These assertions exercise the T-041 bounded-host-memory control for the write-behind pipeline ("bounded host Data in the write-behind donation pipeline; refusal/drop preserves live serving") and the availability side of TB-007. The test does not weaken any security control. It uses distinct cache scopes (tenant-a..e), consistent with the salt-scoping posture in T-041(d), and no real keys or secrets. Test hooks (afterPublishBeforeIndexForTesting, fixture.startDonation) are existing test-only surface that this unit does not alter. Remaining limits: the patch excerpt was truncated, and the fixture helpers (startDonation with receipt/scope, makeStore(donationRecorder:)) and the Barrier support are defined in other files outside this unit, so their correctness was not verified here. Nothing in the visible evidence invalidates a threat-model assumption or introduces new attack surface.
